newsitem.title: USA: Titan secures Orphan Drug status.
newsitem.headline: Titan secures Orphan Drug status.

text.p: Titan Pharmaceuticals Inc said Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted Orphan Drug status for its product Spheramine.
Spheramine is being developed for the treatment of later stage Parkinson's disease.
Orphan Drug designations are given to drugs that treat medical conditions affecting 200,000 people or less, and for which adequate cures or treatments do not exist.

Spheramine consists of microcarriers coated with dopamine-producing natural human cells. The product is targeted at patients afflicted with Parkinson's disease, a progressively degenerative neurological disease in which specialized brain cells that produce the neurotransmitter, dopamine, slowly die.

Spheramine uses natural human cells that can be made using cell culture techniques. Pilot animal studies have indicated the effectiveness of Spheramine in reversing disease symptoms in a rat model of Parkinson's disease.
Studies have been started in non-human primates, and clinical trials are expected to start in late stage Parkinson's patients in 1998.
